transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi. Um... I'm just having some trouble at work lately. I'm a nurse, and... I just keep losing my train of thought on the floor. Like, if an IV pump beeps, or... or someone asks another nurse a question, I just completely forget what patient flow issue I was working on. It's... yeah. That's mainly why I'm here.
Have you had trouble with focus or attention like this since childhood?

Um... yeah, I guess so. Even back in elementary school, my teachers used to write that I was... bright, but careless. I was always losing worksheets or just forgetting to turn my homework in. My mom actually had to sit with me every night just to... keep me on track.
Have these attention problems also been causing difficulties outside of work, such as at home or in your personal life?

Um... yeah, I suppose so. Just... forgetting things that should be routine, I guess. Like, I'll mean to call a family member back, or... pay a bill at home, and it just slips my mind. Sometimes I even don't show up for appointments. Even when I really meant to go, or... even after I set a reminder, it just doesn't happen. So... yeah.
Before these work problems got worse, were you having the same kinds of attention and forgetfulness difficulties throughout your life?

Um... well, it's always been there, like I said. But... it really became a big issue when I got promoted. I took on charge-nurse duties, um... almost two years ago now. That's when it just... got a lot harder to manage.
Do you find yourself feeling excessively worried or on edge most days?
Um... no, not really. I mean... I get stressed about work, sure. But I don't think I'm... excessively worried about things in general. Just... normal stress, I guess.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days lately?
Um... no. Not really. I mean, I'm frustrated with myself, but... I wouldn't say I'm depressed.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, predominantly inattentive presentation, with clear lifelong inattention beginning in childhood, persistent problems with forgetfulness and losing track of tasks, and impairment across work and home settings. Symptoms worsened with increased occupational demands but were present well before that change. Generalized anxiety and depressive disorder were considered but the patient denied excessive worry or persistent depressed mood.
